Sports.title: Ruben Amorim jokes Manchester United is ‘more boring’ without him in cheeky interaction
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim jokes Manchester United is ‘more boring’ without him in cheeky interaction

Ruben Amorim joked that Manchester United's press conferences are 'more boring' without him on Saturday evening.

Amorim, who is now in charge of AC Milan, beat his former side 4-2 in a pre-season friendly before laughing with journalists.

2 Amorim led AC Milan to a 4-2 win over Man United before he cracked a cheeky joke Credit: AFP

The Portuguese boss was sacked as Man United manager in January, with Darren Fletcher and then Michael Carrick taking over.

He departed the club following a very tough tenure, during which he won just 25 of his 63 games in all competitions.

Amorim was often slammed for his stubborn tactical approach, as he remained committed to a 3-4-2-1 set-up for United.

But it was that formation that put Carrick's Red Devils to the sword on Saturday, as Milan came out on top.

And after the win, Amorim was in such a good mood that he laughed along with some English journalists as he left the stadium.

What did Ruben Amorim say?

Amorim stopped to shake hands with journalist Simon Stone, as well as some other media professionals at the ground.

He chuckled and asked: "Do you miss me?"

To which one person replied: "We miss your press conferences!"

And that led to the former Man United boss hysterically laughing and joking: "They're more boring now!"

As he walked away, he continued to chuckle and pose for some pictures with fans before entering the Milan team bus.

2 Amorim joked about press conferences at Man United in a funny interaction Credit: Getty

Amorim's entertaining press conferences

Amorim's joke didn't seem to be a dig at new Man United boss Carrick, but more of a quip aimed at himself.

The 41-year-old was sacked as Red Devils manager just 24 hours after making a bombshell statement towards the club's board during his final press conference in his post.

He also went on to storm out of the explosive conference in January, in a chat that certainly wasn't boring.

On top of that, Amorim had many other interesting press conference moments during his time in Manchester.

Amorim was often very honest when speaking to the media, calling his own team the 'worst in the club's history' last year.

He admitted that he could be sacked at the end of 2024 too, following a third straight defeat during that season.

So, he's definitely not wrong that the United press room has lost of bit of spark, for journalists in particular, since his exit.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala collapses during game in scary scenes as Bayern Munich chief issues update
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala collapses during game in scary scenes as Bayern Munich chief issues update

Jamal Musiala collapsed on the pitch during Bayern Munich's game against RB Leipzig on Saturday in scary scenes.

The Germany international had to be caught by teammate Ismael Saibari as he began to look unsteady on his feet.



4 Musiala had to be caught as he collapsed to the ground on Saturday Credit: Getty

As the Telekom Cup Final clash moved towards the last five minutes, Musiala appeared to be struggling in the intense heat.

With temperatures soaring at 33 degrees Celsius, he began to look disorientated and wobbled as he stood on the pitch.

The worrying moment came after he scored Bayern's third goal in their 3-1 win, as he waited for the game to restart.



While standing still, Musiala became unsteady and started falling in stages, with Saibari rushing over to help him out.

The Moroccan managed to get to him quickly and helped him lie down on the grass, with Joshua Kimmich rushing over too.



Bayern's medical team then charged onto the pitch to provide some treatment as the 23-year-old concerningly lay still.

Fortunately, after a few minutes, the medical staff confirmed that Musiala was okay and nothing serious had occurred.



He was then clapped off the pitch after standing up and being helped to the touchline, and fans chanted his name.

What is the latest on Musiala?

Speaking post-match, Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer said: "It will become clear what it was. But of course we are keeping our fingers crossed."

And thankfully, it has been confirmed that Musiala is okay after the incident, with sporting director Max Eberl providing an update.

4 Saibari rushed over to help his teammate after spotting him struggling Credit: Getty



4 Medics then rushed onto the pitch to treat him in scary scenes Credit: Getty

4 Thankfully, he was okay and has been confirmed to be doing well Credit: Getty

Eberl said to the media in the mixed zone: "The most important thing, he's doing well!"

It has also since been reported in Germany that Musiala complained of dizziness and circulatory problems due to the heat.



Initial examinations by Bayern have revealed nothing so far following the concerning moment.

Musiala is expected to rest and recover over the next few days.

But he will now be a doubt for the start of the season in Germany, with Bayern taking on Borussia Dortmund in the DFL Super Cup next weekend.

The Bundesliga champions then kickstart their league campaign against Stuttgart on Friday, August 28.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce release furious statement amid surprise links to Chelsea star
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce have released a statement angrily denying rumours that the club are interested in signing Chelsea star Jamie Gittens.

Gittens had been linked to a potential move to the Turkish giants this summer, only a year since arriving in the Premier League.

3 Fenerbahce have denied that they are looking at signing Gittens Credit: Getty

The English winger made 27 appearances for the Blues after joining from Borussia Dortmund for a £51.5million total fee.

But after a tough first season at Stamford Bridge, talk of a switch to Turkey arose and started to spread on social media.

That was something that Fenerbahce had also gotten wind of - and they made sure to put an end to any links instantly.

They released a statement on Saturday to deny any interest in Gittens, slamming the 'false' claims regarding the player.

Fenerbahce's angry statement

"Reports circulating in some media outlets today regarding our club's interest in Chelsea FC player Jamie Gittens are completely unfounded and do not reflect the truth," Fenerbahce wrote.

"We once again clearly state that attempts to manipulate Fenerbahçe Sports Club through false transfer claims and artificially created agendas will have no effect.

"Fenerbahçe conducts its sporting structure, transfer policy, and future planning in all branches, especially football, in accordance with its own strategy, needs, and established programs.

"Therefore, we expect this approach of using our club's name to create public opinion and steer Fenerbahçe towards certain directions to cease.

"Our sole focus right now is our match against Gençlerbirliği in the first week of the Trendyol Super League.

"We respectfully request that our great Fenerbahçe fans disregard such unfounded news and continue their support for our teams only by considering the statements made through our club's official channels."

3 Gittens hasn't played a competitive game for Chelsea since January Credit: Getty

Gittens' Chelsea stats

Gittens' time as a Chelsea player has not gone how he would have wanted after making his big-money move from Germany.

In his 27 appearances last season, he only scored one goal and provided five assists across all competitions.

His tough first year at Stamford Bridge was interrupted by injury, as he missed more than 100 days with a hamstring issue.

He sat out of 22 games for the Blues in total, with his last competitive appearance for the club coming on January 31.

New manager Xabi Alonso certainly has a decision to make on the future of Gittens heading into the new campaign.

But he appears to be a fan of the 22-year-old, playing him in five of Chelsea's six pre-season friendlies so far this summer.

3 The Englishman's Chelsea career has been hampered by injury so far Credit: Getty

Gittens has one goal and one assist to his name under Alonso, showing that he can make an impact.

And after links to Fenerbahce were spectacularly shut down, he could feature in the squad for Chelsea's Premier League opener against Fulham on Monday, August 24.

talkSPORT will have live coverage from Craven Cottage, with commentary coming from Sam Matterface and former England midfielder Danny Murphy.

Sports.title: Taiwo Awoniyi to leave Nottingham Forest for Premier League rivals as deal agreed
Sports.content:
Taiwo Awoniyi to leave Nottingham Forest for Premier League rivals as deal agreed

Nottingham Forest striker Taiwo Awoniyi is set to leave the club after four years to join Coventry City, talkSPORT understands.

Awoniyi, who signed for Forest in 2022, has permission to undergo a medical ahead of a £17million move to Coventry.



3 Awoniyi has played over 100 games for Forest but he's set to leave for Coventry Credit: Getty

The Nigeria international will leave the City Ground on a permanent transfer, just a week before the start of the new season.

Coventry manager Frank Lampard is said to have had a big say in signing the forward, pushing to get a move over the line.

Awoniyi has featured regularly for Forest during pre-season, scoring one goal under new boss Oliver Glasner in recent weeks.



But he is now set to depart following a 45-minute appearance against Bayer Leverkusen in what was the club's final friendly.

Awoniyi on the move

Awoniyi was not guaranteed to be playing first-team football under Glasner this season, due to his many attacking options.



Chris Wood, Igor Jesus, Dan Ndoye and Arnaud Kalimuendo are all players who can lead the line for Forest.

So, the 29-year-old forward is making a move to their Midlands rivals, joining up with Lampard and Coventry.



Awoniyi will depart Forest after making 103 appearances for the club, scoring 23 goals and providing six assists altogether.

Last season, he played 17 Premier League games but started just three, scoring four goals and setting up one.

He was also left out of their Europa League squad, sitting out of all of their games played on the continent.

3 Lampard is said to have pushed for Coventry to sign Awoniyi from Forest Credit: Getty



Coventry's summer business so far

Championship winners Coventry have already made six summer signings, breaking their transfer record multiple times.

Ahead of the Premier League campaign, midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi joined the club for £23.1million from Nordsjaelland.

Yirenkyi's move broke the Sky Blues' record, just as Carl Rushworth's permanent switch from Brighton did beforehand.

They have also re-signed Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United and added Loum Tchaouna and Aurele Amenda to the squad.



Frank Onyeka has also joined permanently from Brentford.

£17m Awoniyi is going to be the next through the door, joining Haji Wright, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Ellis Simms in attack.

3 Awoniyi could make his Coventry debut in less than a week's time Credit: Getty

Wright is suffering from an injury heading into the season, having missed Coventry's entire build-up to the campaign.

So, Awoniyi may well see some game time straight after his move if Lampard wants him leading the line.



The Sky Blues take on Premier League champions Arsenal in their opening game on Friday, August 21.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans divided on Enzo Fernandez during first appearance since World Cup and transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Chelsea fans divided on Enzo Fernandez during first appearance since World Cup and transfer deadline

Enzo Fernandez was given a mixed reception on his Chelsea return amid speculation over his future.

The Argentine was handed his first pre-season minutes in Saturday’s 3-1 win over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge.



4 Enzo Fernandez was given a mixed reception on his return to action Credit: Getty

Fans made their feelings clear when he replaced Reece James in the 62nd minute of the game.

As his name was read out over the public address system, a chorus of boos were heard coming from the stands.

Some fans opted to give Fernandez their backing by cheering the star as he stood on the touchline.



Once he had entered the pitch, some fans booed every touch of the ball while others chanted his name.

Fernandez had an eventful summer with Argentina in their run to the World Cup final.



The 25-year-old scored his country’s equalising goal in the semi-final victory over England before being sent off for two reckless bookings in the World Cup final defeat to Spain.

What next for Fernandez?

Fernandez told Chelsea in May of his desire to leave the club.

It was understood at the time that his preference was to move to Real Madrid.



But his hopes of a move to the Spanish capital were dashed last month, when the La Liga giants issued a statement saying that they were not planning on signing the star.

That had initially left Fernandez in limbo but recent interest from Manchester City could still see the star depart Stamford Bridge this summer.

4 The Argentine was quickly back into the thick of it as Chelsea skipper Credit: Getty

Chelsea slapped a £120million price tag on the Argentine while giving City a deadline of 5pm on Friday to table a bid, but no offers were received.



Chelsea, under the guidance of new head coach Xabi Alonso, are now planning to start the season with Fernandez as a key part of their plans.

Meanwhile, £117m record signing Morgan Rogers scored on his Stamford Bridge debut with a close-range finish after Joao Pedro’s header was saved by Real Sociedad goalkeeper Alex Remiro.

The Brazilian striker proved decisive during the Blues’ final pre-season fixture, netting twice on a positive afternoon for Alonso’s side.

Alonso pleased with his side's display

"It was a very good last preparation game," Alonso told the club's media after the match.



"For some players it was the first one and the last one. For us, there were some good things, some things we can improve. It’s normal at this moment for some players.

4 Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso took charge of his first game at Stamford Bridge on Saturday Credit: Getty

4 Morgan Rogers opened his account for Chelsea with a goal against the La Liga side Credit: AFP

"It was great to have all the team together. Some of them after three days could play for 60 minutes.



"It was the last test. Now we have a whole week to prepare for Fulham, but it was a good feeling in the stadium."

Next up for Chelsea is their opening Premier League clash at Craven Cottage on Monday, August 24 – live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: ‘Do me a favour’ – Controversial Championship goal sparks furious VAR rant
Sports.content:
Adrian Durham slammed the suggestion that VAR should be introduced in the EFL after a controversial West Brom goal.

The Baggies opened the scoring against Norwich City on Saturday with a goal that went in via an 'obvious' handball.

3 Heggebo scored for West Brom against Norwich with his hand on Saturday afternoon Credit: Getty

Aune Heggebo bundled the ball over the line to put his side 1-0 up in the 75th minute of the game following a whipped cross from ex-Chelsea youngster Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

But replays showed that the Norwegian striker managed to score thanks to the cross coming off his arm in the box.

Norwich's defenders appealed for the goal to be ruled out, with referee Tim Robinson waving them away and Heggebo sprinting off to the corner to celebrate his first of the campaign.

During talkSPORT's live commentary at Carrow Road, Dean Ashton explained: "It looked a handball, but his arms are close to his body...

"You can usually sense from players' reactions what they've seen and, in particular, Jose Cordoba, as soon as the ball went in, he was remonstrating with the referee. He felt it was handball and Ben Chrisene was doing the same.

"We've seen a replay and it absolutely is a handball. It's quite incredible actually, it's so obvious. It's as clear as you like from Heggebo, he almost uses two hands to poke it in.

"No wonder Norwich are frustrated."

And following the incident, talkSPORT commentator Mike Sewell suggested that VAR could be of use in the Championship to prevent moments such as the one involving Heggebo again.

Adrian Durham's VAR rant

But just the mere mention of VAR being introduced to the EFL was something that left presenter Adrian Durham furious.

In reaction to Sewell's comments, Durham said: "Oh, do shut up.

3 Durham didn't agree with the suggestion that VAR should be introduced due to the error at Carrow Road Credit: Getty

"Philippe Clement [Norwich manager] called for VAR last season...when things are going wrong.

"They've had all this time. How long have they had? 70-odd minutes to score and they haven't.

"So they've had a bit of bad luck? It doesn't mean you need to bring in VAR, literally no players and fans want VAR in the Championship.

"Do me a favour. Ridiculous. What is he talking about?"

What did Clement say post-match?

Speaking to talkSPORT about the handball post-match, Norwich boss Clement said: "We had a conversation about it [with the officials].

"They didn't see, so that's disappointing. I understand that in moments it's hard to see things, but the position that the linesman is in that moment, he needs to see that clearly.

3 Norwich went on to lose their Championship opener 2-1 to West Brom Credit: Getty

"It's disappointing to lose at least two points, maybe three points, to a decision like that...and also after that, several players go to the referee and if nothing happened, why would they do that?"

How did Norwich vs West Brom finish?

Heggebo's goal with 15 minutes to play was a controversial one, but Durham wasn't too bothered about the missed handball.

Clement was though, as just before the 90-minute mark, his side went on to concede again, this time to Morgan.

Norwich did get a late goal back via Mathias Kvistgaarden, but it wasn't enough and they were beaten on Saturday.

The Canaries won't be happy with the manner in which they lost, having had 20 shots and an xG of almost three goals.

West Brom scored two of their eight shots on goal, with their goalkeeper, Max O'Leary, making seven saves in total.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as team-mate rushes over to catch Germany star
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as team-mate rushes over to catch Germany star

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Bayern Munich and Germany star Jamal Musiala appeared to pass out during his side's friendly win over RB Leipzig, sparking concern among players and fans.

The midfielder had just scored to make it 3-1 to his side in the 81st minute, but appeared dazed and confused just two minutes later before he was caught by new team-mate Ismael Saibari.

After the Morocco star lowered him to the ground, medical staff rushed onto the field as Bayern players surrounded the 23-year-old.

Amid a hush from the crowd, the medical staff eventually gave a thumbs up, with reports in Germany suggesting that Musiala had struggled with the 33 degrees Celsius heat.

Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer said after the game: 'It will become clear what it was. But of course we are keeping our fingers crossed.'

Director of sport Max Eberl, meanwhile, said: 'He is fine, and that is the most important thing.'

Jamal Musiala appeared to faint during Bayern Munich's pre-season friendly victory

New footage emerged after the incident to show Musiala looking uncomfortable just after scoring his goal, and two minutes later he had collapsed.

The incident comes following a debate around hydration breaks, which were held regularly during the World Cup.

Bayern, meanwhile, won the game 3-1, with Luis Diaz, Nathaniel Brown and Musiala on the scoresheet.

Musiala, who played at the World Cup with Germany, had only been introduced as a 69th minute substitute, but had to leave the field of play soon after.

England captain Harry Kane was not involved in the game but returned to training alongside the likes of Michael Olise this week.

Bayern kick off their competitive season next weekend in the German Super Cup, when they will take on Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: West Brom star sparks controversy with handball goal in Championship opening day win - leaving opposing manager livid
Sports.content:
West Brom star sparks controversy with handball goal in Championship opening day win - leaving opposing manager livid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

West Brom star Aune Heggebo left fans stunned as he scored with his hand on the opening day – with officials missing the offence.

The Baggies were well below par in their 2-1 victory over Norwich at Carrow Road on Saturday afternoon, but managed to claim victory following strikes from Heggebo and new signing Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

It was a far from routine win for James Morrison's side, and the main takeaway from the game was Heggebo's opening goal, which clearly came off his arm.

The Norway forward raced in to tap home Morgan's cross, but, as he raised his leg to try and poke it in, he raised his arms too.

The ball struck his left arm and fell into the net, with Norwich players protesting to referee Tim Robinson – who missed the incident.

Heggebo wheeled away in celebration, with none of the officials noticing he had in fact committed an offence to score.

Aune Heggebø’s goal for West Bromwich Albion against Norwich City has fuelled controversy over an alleged handball.



Should the goal have stood? 💭 pic.twitter.com/TcKQ4ctV9N — ITV Football (@itvfootball) August 15, 2026

West Brom star Aune Heggebo stunned fans with a handball goal on the opening day of the Championship season

'It was clearly with the arm that the player scores – we could see that from where we were watching, 50 yards away,' Norwich manager Philippe Clement said after the game. 'It was the decisive moment in the game and should have been spotted.

'There are four officials and one of them should have seen it. Maybe the referee didn't have the best view – but the linesman on our side needs to see that. Missing game-changing moments like this shouldn't happen – it has cost us at least two, maybe three points.'

Morgan, who joined for £4million from Chelsea this summer, added a second goal in the 87th minute, with Mathias Kvistgaarden's 90th minute goal proving to be nothing but a consolation.

Fans on social media were left stunned by the incident, with one writing: 'Cracking header from Heggebo tbf.'

Another wrote: 'You could see it on Aune Heggebo after the goal that he had cheated, and it's just unbelievable that neither the referee nor linesman sees this.

'I'll take one of these in every single match this season over VAR anyway.'

Sports.title: Babar Azam injury concerns, an awkward captaincy change and usual off-field maelstrom - Pakistan mirror England's chaos and Test series will be packed with drama
Sports.content:
Babar Azam injury concerns, an awkward captaincy change and usual off-field maelstrom - Pakistan mirror England's chaos and Test series will be packed with drama

Unlock more of the best of our cricket coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

New captain, interim coach, players recalled who had not previously featured in 2026. If England’s lot this summer befell Pakistan, it would be considered par for the course.

This coming week, with incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming not ready to take up his role, Joe Root and Marcus Trescothick will form a temporary leadership alliance, while Dan Lawrence, Ollie Pope and Sam Cook return to the fray in Leeds.

England are desperate to create some stability after reaching the end of the Bazball era with the midsummer departures of Ben Stokes and Brendon McCullum, but if one team in world cricket is accustomed to dealing with the unsettling elements of wholesale change it is Pakistan.

Some will even argue that rather than run from chaos, they embrace it, and in keeping with dull moments being conspicuous by their absence where their cricket is involved, captain Babar Azam provided a pre-series scare on Friday when he was forced to retire hurt and pull out of the remainder of the warm-up match against a County Select XI.

Failing to ride a rising delivery from Hampshire’s teenage seamer Manny Lumsden, Babar was struck on the right glove and immediately began wringing his hand in discomfort.

Team insiders insist the removal was a precautionary measure and that although there was no sign of a fracture, the fact that it was the same middle finger Pakistan’s premier batsman damaged during the recent Test win over West Indies in Trinidad meant no chances were being taken.

Babar Azam, pictured earlier this year ahead of a Test against West Indies, gave his side an injury scare this week ahead of the England clash at Headingley

That eight-wicket victory earlier this month was Pakistan’s first overseas for three years, ending a sequence of eight straight defeats, and although Babar’s brief sidelining removed the chance to further develop the on-field bond between this latest combination of players, he is pencilled in to rejoin them in the nets at Headingley on Monday, 48 hours before the first Test of three begins.

Mirroring the situation England found themselves in, a level of awkwardness surrounded Pakistan’s most recent captaincy change ahead of the 1-1 series draw in the Caribbean.

The strong friendship between Joe Root and Harry Brook has diluted the issue from an English perspective after Stokes nominated the latter as his successor during his farewell at Trent Bridge, and Brook followed up with a public pitch to become captain across all formats.

Arguably, Pakistan had to overcome something slightly worse, though, with Shan Masood axed after three years in charge but retained in the XI under Babar. The response offered mixed results: although Masood scored a first-innings hundred, the match ended in defeat and him nursing a finger injury that would keep him out of the second match.

It was partly for his statesmanlike demeanour that Masood replaced Babar as captain in 2023 and it is for his diplomatic communication skills that former captain Rashid Latif suggested this week a novel relationship could now develop. Masood, he argued, should continue with media interactions, shielding Babar and allowing him to concentrate on directing operations in the middle now he has the armband back.

‘An England tour is a difficult assignment, and the English media often tries to unnecessarily involve visiting teams in news stories,’ he claimed.

To be fair, previous Pakistan teams touring here this century have provided plenty of material of their own. Think back to Inzamam-ul-Haq walking his team off the field and forfeiting The Oval Test amid ball tampering accusations from officials in 2006 or the spot-fixing scandal that grubbed the series four years later as examples.

But Latif’s desire for Babar to concentrate on lifting Pakistan’s Test cricket out of the doldrums is well meaning. Languishing in eighth in the current World Test Championship standings, one place below England, they have won just one of their previous eight series - against Stokes’ side in the autumn of 2024.

Shan Masood (left) was stripped of the captaincy but is still in the team under Azam (right)

And dealing with the off-field maelstrom in a cricket-mad country is never easy. Just this week, Shaheen Shah Afridi was batting away suggestions that Babar will be replacing him as Pakistan’s one-day captain imminently. There is also talk of Salman Ali Agha making way in Twenty20.

In Pakistani cricket circles, there is always someone ready to take your job. When Agha was appointed last year, he became his country’s fourth T20 captain in 14 months.

The same goes with coaches. Sarfaraz Ahmed leads this tour, but only after surviving calls for his head following the 2-0 defeat to Bangladesh. He only moved into the post in April.

Gary Kirsten, the man who guided India to the No 1 Test ranking and 2011 World Cup glory, lasted only six months in charge of Pakistan’s white-ball teams during 2024.

Jason Gillespie, their other high-profile foreign appointment in a split coaching set-up, didn’t stick around much longer.

Both were upset by external interference in team affairs, with Gillespie refusing to let success against England during the 2-1 home win two years ago cloud his judgment. He had been reduced to a ‘match-day analyst’, he said, adding that ‘it wasn’t what I signed up for.’

Whatever happens over the next month, those investing emotions in a series like this are unlikely to be disappointed by the drama that unfolds.

Past Pakistan dramas:

2001: England’s attempts to save a match at Old Trafford, and thereby win a fifth series in a row, were marred by Pakistan taking four wickets with no balls. The umpiring errors from David Shepherd and Ed Nichols, in the days before technology was used automatically to check bowlers overstepping, helped Pakistan to a win with less than seven overs remaining. Three of the officiating errors came at the legendary Shepherd’s end, with Saqlain Mushtaq the benefactor.

2006: Inzamam-ul-Haq became the first captain in 129 years to forfeit a Test match after taking umbrage at being punished for ball-tampering on the fourth day of the Oval Test. What began as a five-run penalty imposed by the umpires - Australian Darrell Hair and Billy Doctrove, of West Indies - soon escalated into a major diplomatic incident, with Pakistan refusing to take the field after tea, leading to Hair removing the bails and England being declared winners in the record books.

Inzamam-ul-Haq is pictured in 2006 - the Pakistan captain forfeited after a ball-tampering scandal

2010: The actions of three of Pakistan's best players - captain Salman Butt, along with bowlers Mohammad Amir and Mohammad Asif - shook the sporting world following a newspaper sting that showed them to be participating in a betting scam known as spot-fixing.

Amir’s brilliance had England on the ropes at 102 for seven before Jonathan Trott and Stuart Broad produced a Test record eighth-wicket stand of 332. Both their achievement, and England’s innings victory, were inevitably tarnished when it emerged no-balls had been delivered to order for cash. All three men were jailed and handed lengthy bans from cricket.

2016: Lord’s was a much happier place this time as veteran captain Misbah-ul-Haq led the tourists to a 75-run win remembered for his reaction to his 10th Test hundred. To mark the 154-ball effort, the 42-year-old dropped his bat and peeled off 10 press-ups, in tribute to the army officers who had put the Pakistan squad through their paces pre-tour. The fitness regime was acknowledged again by the entire squad post-match, with a group press-up celebration.

Sports.title: Named: The Premier League club whose fans will have to fork out nearly £5,000 to follow their team this season - as staggering new data reveals where every side ranks, with surprise No 1
Sports.content:
Named: The Premier League club whose fans will have to fork out nearly £5,000 to follow their team this season - as staggering new data reveals where every side ranks, with surprise No 1

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

'Football without fans is nothing,' the great Celtic manager Jock Stein once said.

Looking at the state of modern matchday prices, which are pricing out droves of loyal supporters, those words have rarely felt truer.

New data has revealed that it could cost £5,000 to follow the most expensive team in the Premier League this season home and away - and that's a conservative estimate.

The unlucky fanbase is that of Bournemouth, whose followers would have to shell out £4,911.61 to watch them home and away this coming campaign without a season ticket. That includes extortionate train costs, plus a pie and two pints at every game, and a replica kit.

The second and third-most expensive are Sunderland and Newcastle - all three place so high because of their extreme geographies, meaning the travel costs rack up.

By contrast, the cheapest club to follow would be Brentford with a season ticket, but that still comes to £2,827.26 when you price in travel, grub, and alcoholic fare.

The costliest 'Big Six' team to follow is Arsenal, who are the fourth-most expensive club to watch with or without a season ticket.

Bournemouth are the most expensive team to follow in the Premier League if you factor in ticket costs, travel prices, food and drink, and a jersey

Tracking the Gunners home and away would set you back £3,748.56 with a season ticket and £4,349.06 without - the sort of money Bukayo Saka earns in two-and-a-half hours.

By comparison, the other 'Big Six teams' are quite cheap to follow.

While Tottenham's ticket prices are second only to Arsenal, overall they are the ninth-most-dear team to follow thanks to London's national train connections.

Meanwhile, Manchester United come in 12th, Liverpool are 14th, Chelsea rank 16th, and Manchester City place 17th, arguably showing a stronger value for money.

Only Coventry, Leeds, and Brentford would be cheaper to follow as a whole package than City, who will set back fans £3,059.22 with a season ticket and £3,424.22 without.

Alright, then, you ask, where can I fill my stomach the cheapest?

The answer to that is Hull, where a pie costs a reasonable £3 - 20 pence cheaper than their nearest competitors in Hull City.

Every other club will charge you over £4, most will hit you for more than £5, and Arsenal have the audacity to demand £8.85, according to last season's menu.

Being one of Arsenal's victorious supporters comes at a price - they've got the costliest tickets in the Premier League

If you're looking to wet your whistle with a couple of beers, it's Ipswich where you can do that on the cheap, for just £3.50.

Coventry (£3.60) and Hull (£.90) are the next-cheapest, though they could raise their fares for the coming campaign.

Arsenal are once again the culprits in this department, asking their supporters for £6.80 per pint, though most things do cost more in London generally.

It wouldn't be right to follow your team home and away without a little bit of merchandise, so how about a replica men's shirt for the 2026-27 campaign?

You're in luck, Hull faithful, as your kits come out the most affordable at £64. Ipswich, Brentford, and Crystal Palace trail closely on £65.

Tottenham - whose performances in recent seasons few people would actually want to replicate - are the most expensive to imitate in the stands.

They have the brass neck to ask for £90 for a replica kit, though Chelsea are hot on their heels at £89.99.

Overall, the average cost of following your club with a season ticket, with trains, pints, pies, and a replica kit thrown in, costs £3,450.56 in the Premier League.

Brentford are the cheapest team to follow, partly thanks to London's good transport links

Doing so without a season ticket - which, in fairness, few people would do in totality - raises that financial sacrifice to £3,902.44.

It is little wonder that we see regular protests against clubs' ticket prices, and similarly constant grumblings about the cost of rail travel in this country.

Fans are gouged another £730 if they sign up to every broadcasting platform available in the United Kingdom to watch Premier League games - and that doesn't even give you access to every game.

In Singapore, viewers are able to watch all 380 matches on Premier League + for a monthly payment of £25.

Where would football be without the fans, eh?

Sports.title: Aston Villa in talks with Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki as PSG move crumbles, and West Ham break Championship transfer record for Arne Engels: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa plot swoop for Suzuki as PSG deal crumbles

Aston Villa have rekindled talks for Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki after the collapse of his move to Paris Saint-Germain.

The Japan international was scheduled to have a medical with PSG today but the French club indicated the commission demanded by agents, was considered too high and the deal fell through.

Zion Suzuki has rekindled talks with Aston Villa after his Paris Saint-Germain move fell through

Villa have Emiliano Martinez as their number one who was expected to stay after the World Cup but had been a target for Juventus.

The Italians fell short in their initial offers for Martinez and have been discussing a loan for Guglielmo Vicario from Tottenham and Ederson at Fenerbahce.

Villa, meanwhile, are wrapping up the signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atletico Madrid, and Halmstad BK have expressed their interest in Villa striker Rory Wilson.

City close to Bouaddi deal

Manchester City are close to concluding talks for Lille’s £85million-rated midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi as Barcelona press to sign Rodri.

Bouaddi, the 18-year-old Morocco international, started on the bench for Lille in their friendly at Everton yesterday and coach Davide Ancelotti confirmed negotiations.

Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now, which is expected to come at a premium.

'Of course, there are negotiations,' admitted Ancelotti. 'There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us!

'He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18-years-old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch. He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.'

The teenager's arrival at City would help offset the loss of Spain captain Rodri who is set in a move to Barcelona.

The Spanish champions have made a third proposal worth around £60m for the 30-year-old and hope that City agree on a compromise to sell.

City maintain an interest in midfielder Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea's Friday's deadline passing without the necessary £120m bid being made. Tottenham are also expected to make an offer for City winger Savinho.

Newcastle's talks progress with Benfica's Dedic

Newcastle are advancing in talks to sign Bosnia right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica.

Talks are continuing over a £30million fee for the 23-year-old and he is expected to arrive on Tyneside on Sunday.

The 23-year-old played under coach Matthias Jaissle at RB Salzburg.

Newcastle have also considered going back into the market for Bayern Munich's Joao Palhinha as they search for a midfielder.

Palhinha has interest from Aston Villa and Benfica but Bayern only want a permanent sale not a loan.

Newcastle are advancing in talks to sign Bosnia right-back Amar Dedic from Benfica

Spurs reach agreement with Boro for Phillips

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips is ready to complete his protracted move to Middlesbrough.

The deal was held up last weekend after concerns over his medical. However, following further tests and discussions, the clubs have reached an agreement.

He is due on Teesside this weekend to finalise his switch to the Riverside.

Boro kick off their Championship campaign at home to Lincoln City today.

Tottenham defender Ashley Phillips is ready to complete his protracted move to Middlesbrough

Coventry bolster attack

Coventry City are in talks with Fenerbahce over a £21million deal for striker Sidiki Cherif.

As well as agreeing to sign Nottingham Forest's Taiwo Awoniyi, manager Frank Lampard wants Cherif who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January.

The 19-year-old scored three goals in 14 games for Fenerbahce.

Benfica offer for Harwood-Bellis rejected

Southampton have rejected a £17.5million offer from Benfica for defender Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The Portuguese side, coached by Marco Silva, turned to the 24-year-old after initial interest in Chelsea's Tosin Adarabioyo who wants to stay at Stamford Bridge.

Benfica are considering an improved offer with Harwood-Bellis interested in the move.

Benfica are considering an improved offer for Saints' Harwood-Bellis after having their initial bid of £17.5million rejected, while the 24-year-old is interested in the move

Forest sign former Fulham goalkeeper Benda

Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of former Fulham goalkeeper Steven Benda.

The 27-year-old is being brought in to replace the departed Angus Gunn as third-choice. He had spells on loan at Feyenoord and Millwall last season.

Eagles sign £21m right back Khalaili

Crystal Palace have completed the £21million signing of Union Saint-Gilloise full-back Anan Khalaili.

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend.

The 21-year-old is being brought in to provide competition for Daniel Munoz at right wing-back.

However, there is no guarantee that the £20m-rated Colombian will stay beyond this summer amid interest from the likes of Tottenham and Everton. He has two years left on his deal.

Khalaili, who has won 16 caps for Israel, said: 'I'm happy to be here, I'm excited, and I can't wait to start.

'I’ve followed the Premier League. It's a new challenge for me, and I've followed Crystal Palace for a long time. I'm happy to be here.'

Khalaili's move to Inter Milan fell through earlier this summer over a health issue, but he passed his medical with Palace last weekend

Gourna-Douath 'excited' to join Tigers

Hull City have finalised the £3.5m transfer of French defensive midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath from RB Salzburg.

The deal is worth £2.9m guaranteed, plus add-ons and a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

The 23-year-old has signed a five-year contract, becoming the club’s 10th summer signing.

Gourna-Douath said: 'I’m really happy because it was such a long journey from the first phone call until I signed. I’m so excited to get started.

'I’m really happy to have this experience. I got a chance to play in the Champions League, Serie A and Ligue 1.

'I've learned a lot and I’m really happy to put this experience on the pitch in the Premier League. The Premier League is the dream of all footballers. Now, I have a chance to play in the Premier League, so I am excited to play.'

Leeds agree £6.8m move for Eveldi

Leeds United have agreed a fee with Borussia Monchengladbach for Nico Elvedi.

The deal is understood to be worth an initial £6.8m plus add-ons.

The central defender was left out of Gladbach’s squad for today’s friendly against Aston Villa.

His arrival would open the door for Sebastiaan Bornauw to join Hamburg.

Gladbach have also negotiated a 15 per cent sell-on.

Black Cats ink Methalie deal

Sunderland have reached a full agreement with Toulouse to sign 20-year-old full-back Dayann Methalie.

The fee is understood to be £26million including add ons.

Methalie has agreed a five-year contract.

West Ham break Championship record for Engels

West Ham have signed Belgium international Arne Engels from Celtic for a Championship record £22 million.

Engels has joined West Ham on a five-year deal, as the East London side attempt to make an immediate return to the Premier League.

The versatile midfielder adds creativity to the Championship outfit and is renowned for his set-piece delivery.

He is not, however, eligible for their second-tier opener against Burnley tomorrow and will have to wait until next weekend’s home game against Charlton to make his debut.

Celtic have doubled their money on Engels, who they bought from German club Augsburg two years ago.

West Ham have broken the Championship transfer record with the signing of Arne Engels

Engels, capped four times by Belgium, said: ‘It's a really nice project to come into and try to go back to the Premier League. That's the big goal.

‘That’s everybody's goal and it's just up to me to hopefully help the team with it and, together with the supporters, to get some wins.

‘Hopefully, we'll see that it's going to be a good year then and I'm looking forward to the next ones.

‘I'm just looking forward to meeting all the fans at London Stadium. I’m looking forward to this challenging season, but hopefully we can make it a really good one, so let's go for it!’

Sports.title: Golden girl Keely Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as British star loses her 800m European Championship crown with second-place finish - with Olympic champion jokingly removing her medal in disappointed post-race interview
Sports.content:
Audrey Werro is fast becoming an unsolvable riddle for the leading lady of British sport. For the second time in 10 weeks, this Swiss phenomenon left Keely Hodgkinson staring at her heels in a race that lived up to its billing as the best of the European Championships.

To the most talented Audrey since Hepburn went the 800m gold medal. To Hodgkinson, there was presumably no silver lining to be found in finishing a close second on home soil.

If there is to be any consolation, it is that Werro, aged 22, clocked a championship record of 1:54.81 on a chilly, breezy evening in Birmingham to beat her. But warmer thoughts will be harder to find for Hodgkinson.

Instead, the Olympic champion must process the dawning of a serious rivalry and one that is not currently swinging in her favour. This one was settled by the margin of 0.2sec.

In the long run, Hodgkinson might view such moments as the competitive nectar needed for the breaching of new frontiers, of course, but the sting in the present will be real. Not many athletes have the finishing speed to match Hodgkinson, but in their past two races Werro has kicked away from her with the force of a donkey.

The decisive move here came after 500 metres, when Werro put the hammer down.

Hodgkinson, who had been near enough level at the bell after a 56sec opening lap, went with her, and they both separated from Femke Broeders-Bol in third, but the Brit had no answer. She never got her nose in front, and those moments of futility can leave lasting doubts in an athlete.

The 24-year-old, who was chasing a third straight European title, was evidently in little mood to indulge the celebrations of on-track interviewer Iwan Thomas. He assumed she would be thrilled with silver, but Hodgkinson responded: ‘I think I would be happier with a gold.’

Kely Hodgkinson was forced to settle for second in the women's 800m final on Friday

Hodgkinson jokingly took off her silver medal at the European Championships in Birmingham

She later added: ‘I think with that level of competition, any medal is a really good achievement and another one to add to my collection so I can never be disappointed with that. But I'm defending champion so I wanted to do that.

‘I knew it was going to come down to the wire but I really thought I was going to win today. But it wasn't meant to be. I didn't do anything wrong, it was just one of those things.

‘Congrats to Audrey. I am sure we will have more battles.’

That much seems certain. And for two women striving to break the oldest world record in track athletics, that will be a good thing.

But Werro has the edge. Having been beaten twice by Hodgkinson during the indoor portion of the season, she gained spectacular revenge in Stockholm in June when the Brit set a personal best of 1:54.33. Not only was that a win against a full-form Hodgkinson, Werro’s time of 1:53.98 was the third quickest in history. A month later, Werro ran quicker again with a 1:53.80 – if anyone is to better the dubious mark of 1:53.28 set by the Czech Jarmila Kratochvilova in the Eighties, Werro might have the edge.

To think, Werro was only cleared to race in this final on appeal after being tripped in her semi-final. It was a marginal call but also the correct one, so there should be no controversy around what it led to.

For Hodgkinson, the bigger picture will make for strange viewing. After the injury troubles of 2025, her times in 2026 have moved sharply on an upward trajectory, including the indoor world record in February, so she rightly resents any suggestion of ‘failure’ at losing a race or two. She was borderline tetchy in using that label prior to these Championships.

But in athletics, the clock is a secondary adversary to the field and Werro’s emergence is a huge fly in the ointment. For the rest of us watching, we can presumably take great pleasure in where it leads, because athletics needs rivalries. In these two gifted runners, it has one that has the potential to go on for years.

Sports.title: British sprint superstar Amy Hunt claims third European Championships gold as Team GB win the women's AND men's 100m relays - with 'track goddess' on course for historic fourth on Sunday
Sports.content:
Dina Asher-Smith handed a baton to Amy Hunt at 9.52pm on Saturday night and around 31 seconds later, Britain’s newest sprint hero had a third gold medal from these European Championships. The symbolism was almost as blunt as Hunt is quick.

On a chilly evening in Birmingham, when both the host nation’s male and female quartets proved their 4x100m supremacy with victories, it was once again this daughter of Newark who stood tallest in their collective achievements.

For all the sport we have seen in the past week, there is no doubting that the show has been stolen by a 24-year-old who might well have a record-breaking fourth gold before the curtain falls on Sunday night. Given how these relays played out, the jeopardy of the mixed 4x100m, combining the best of both sexes, is distinctly minimal.

The latest gold in Hunt’s set was secured by procession, with Britain’s four of Asher-Smith, Hunt, Success Eduan and Imani Lansiquot annihilating second-placed Switzerland by a full 1.07 sec, crossing in 42.05sec. Who was the fastest of the four women? That would be Hunt, of course.

But let’s add a caveat – when she took the baton on the second leg from her predecessor as Britain’s sprint queen, Asher-Smith, a lead had already been gifted to her. Using those long strides, Hunt then ticked off her stretch in 10.10sec, Eduan built the gap for Lansiquot, and from there the gold was in safe hands.

As with so much around Hunt’s trip to Birmingham, we should add that the big beasts of global sprinting do not live in Europe.

Amy Hunt and her team-mates Success Eduan, Imani-Lara Lansiquot, and Dina Asher-Smith won women's relay gold in Birmingham

Picking up her third gold of this European Championships, Hunt has a historic fourth in sight

To that point, Hunt would be entitled to remind us she already has a world 200m silver medal, but by timings she still has a lot of ground to make up if she is to be a serious player at the LA Olympics in 2028. On this trajectory, with her talent, it should not be ruled out, and nor should we overlook another fact – it was the seventh European gold of Asher-Smith’s career. Hunt may have passed the 30-year-old in the present but not in the historical picture.

But those are thoughts for another day. On this one, Hunt maintained her 100 per cent record in Birmingham as a cog in an eclectic machine. Eduan, for instance, is three weeks away from qualifying as a midwife; Lansiquot has written a play about growing up in Peckham. In tandem, they were devastatingly smooth in their handovers and rapid on the move.

Afterwards, Hunt had some kind words for Asher-Smith, which might be pertinent given the ongoing chatter about whether there has been a peaceful transition of power between domestic rivals.

‘I’m stood next to Dina, she’s the most decorated European athlete in history,’ said Hunt. ‘She has got thousands of medals.

‘I’m stood next to some amazing women. This girl, Success, is a midwife, she brings new babies into the world. Imani, that girl wrote a play.‘That was stunning for it to come together. It’s the time of my life. We have won nearly all of the medals, haven’t we? We have relay camps which mean we can come out here and put on a masterclass from both the teams. So proud of everyone.’

The broader point about the team was relevant – success and failure have often gone hand in hand for British relay quartets. Feast or farce has often been the way.

In Birmingham, the relays followed the pattern of the individual races, with the men’s team of Jeremiah Azu, Louis Hinchliffe, Zharnel Hughes and Romell Glave winning gold a short while earlier.

On the basis that they had both the men’s champion in Glave and his nearest challenger, Azu, the British quartet were always the heavy favourite in the first of the two relays. Their comfort in qualifying fastest for the final only underlined the point.

Asher-Smith handed off the baton to Hunt - but although Hunt is on the ascendancy, her heavily decorated team-mate has the edge in the historical picture

Their triumph came hot on the heels of their male counterparts blowing away the competition (pictured left to right: Zharnel Hughes, Jeremiah Azu, Louie Hinchliffe and Romell Glave)

But it didn’t start well when Azu trailed Italy’s Eric Merek to the first handover. That was unscripted and yet it was corrected by a scorching leg from Louis Hinchcliffe, who saw off his portion in 9.22sec before setting loose the 200m silver medallist Zharnel Hughes with a lead to protect.

With a clean change to Glave, a rapid charge of 9.15sec saw the Brits cross in 38.45sec, 0.19sec clear of Germany with Belgium in third.

Earlier, Jake Heyward slipped from gold to fourth on the final straight in his bid to land a 1500m medal.

For the entirety of the last lap, the Brit was locked in a battle for gold with his team-mate Jake Wightman, but both men succumbed to an astonishing surge across the closing 90m by the giant Dutchman Stefan Nillessen. They were also passed by Samuel Pihlstrom of Sweden and Ireland’s Andrew Coscoran.

Heyward, who was also fourth at the Commonwealth Games, will presumably draw on some perspective by knowing he only returned to racing in the summer after a two-year absence due to multiple surgeries on his Achilles tendon. Running with neither a shoe deal nor a full-time coach, the 27-year-old had threatened one of the most shock results of the championships.

Sports.title: Why a crackdown on set-pieces could leave Arsenal exposed as Mikel Arteta reveals Gunners are looking to adapt to new rules
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta hinted that Arsenal may have to adapt their set-piece routines after an influx of new rules ahead of the upcoming season.

The 2026-27 campaign will feature an unprecedented number of new laws, mostly designed to make the game flow quicker.

These changes will be deployed right through English football this weekend, including Arsenal’s Community Shield match against Manchester City on Sunday.

The laws include countdowns for goal-kicks and throw-ins, time-limited substitutions and a crackdown on holding during set-pieces.

The Gunners have courted attention previously for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules.

On the changes, Arteta said: ‘We have had the Premier League and the referees there with us to explain and go through everything.

Mikel Arteta has hinted Arsenal may have to adapt their approach to set pieces with new rules having been introduced ahead of the new season

Arteta's side attracted attention for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules

‘In pre-season we had the opportunity to see and experience some of them. We will have to see when the season starts and how this unfolds and what is more doable and what is less doable and what we need to adapt.

‘There are a few (which will have a big impact). Not being able to use the towels is already a big one in the Premier League. Let’s see what we do. Maybe we will play with hats on!

‘Something else will come up for sure. We know that everybody is paying so much to the details, all the restarts and the countdowns, that will bring someone else, a different dynamic, different momentum.

‘So I am very curious to see. They are really good rules because what we are doing is trying to promote more game time and the fluidity of the games which is better and hopefully that will work.’

Meanwhile, Arteta said he will have to elevate his level to keep up with the influx of new managers across the Premier League’s Big Six clubs.

The managerial landscape has changed significantly, with Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola at Man City, while Andoni Iraola has taken over from Arne Slot at Liverpool.

Chelsea have also appointed a new manager in Xabi Alonso, who replaced Maresca, and Michael Carrick was handed the permanent job at Manchester United in May.

Tottenham have also turned to Roberto De Zerbi, who took charge at the end of the 2025–26 season.

Arteta added: ‘We will have a lot of challengers looking at the squads, at the managers and at the clubs they are, but we know that.

‘We need to focus on ourselves and making sure that we maximise every resource we have to give ourselves the best chance. Then day by day it is going to be a long, long run.

‘Well, with a few managers as well and some new ones coming into the league that are exceptional. We know this league is full of incredible managers. It is so challenging every week to prepare games against them. That will elevate our level and my level for sure and we will try to be better.’

Sports.title: European Athletics Championships thrown into chaos after 'police incident' in Birmingham
Sports.content:
European Athletics Championships thrown into chaos after 'police incident' in Birmingham

Athletics fans trying to leave Alexander Stadium on Saturday night faced lengthy delays, with West Midlands Police later confirming that a man had been arrested on suspicion of fraud

View 2 Images Fans struggled to get out of Alexander Stadium on Saturday night (Image: Michael Steele/British Athletics via Getty Images)

Medal ceremonies at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were postponed on Saturday evening and transport was suspended after a man was arrested on suspicion of fraud.

‌



Tournament organisers said transport operations had returned to normal in the early hours of Sunday. A statement from Birmingham 2026 read: “Birmingham 2026 can confirm that transport operations have returned to normal following a police incident on Saturday evening.

‌



“Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out whilst West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud. The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships’ family will always be our first priority.

‌



“We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening. Further information will be issued on Sunday relating to the evening’s postponed medal ceremonies.”

A West Midlands Police spokesperson confirmed that a man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of fraud and remained in custody for questioning.

The crowd at the Alexander Stadium appeared to be near its 23,000 capacity to watch Saturday’s evening session, which concluded with Great Britain winning a pair of gold medals in the men’s and women’s 4x100m relays.

‌



At one point during the session, there was an announcement that the six medal ceremonies, scheduled to take place after the final event between 10pm and 11pm, were cancelled. The Press Association understands this decision was taken in relation to the police incident.

Outside, there was a visibly heavy police presence and huge static queues of people waiting for shuttle buses. Alex Ridout wrote on X: “Crazy queues for the shuttle bus after tonight’s European Athletics Championships session.

View 2 Images Britain won gold in the men's and women's 4 x 100 relay on Saturday night (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



“Definitely seems like something has gone on that has potentially caused blockages, with blue flashing lights seen on the main road outside Alexander Stadium.”

Another user, Paul, posted shortly after midnight: “We are one of the last out of the pens. Been queuing since 10.15 with 3 kids who all needed the toilet. In the stadium has been good but the planning on getting out has been abysmal. There was little communication from anyone about the issue!”

Susie Barnacle wrote on X that she had been “waiting for nearly two hours to leave” and described “armed police at the buses”, adding: “We were told precisely nothing!”

Article continues below

Several people on social media said they were told there had been a “security incident”. Michele wrote on X: “What’s happening at the Alexander Stadium? Police saying there’s a security incident and hundreds of people waiting for buses.”

A statement on the event’s official account, posted on X at 11:03pm, read: “We apologise for the significant delays in leaving the Alexander Stadium venue this evening. Buses and coaches will start to arrive and departures will begin to gradually take place.

“We thank you for your patience with this matter. Please listen to the instructions from the safety personnel and marshals who are there to support you.”

Sports.title: Swansea ballboy kicked by Eden Hazard now set to pocket £500m in jaw-dropping deal
Sports.content:
Swansea ballboy kicked by Eden Hazard now set to pocket £500m in jaw-dropping deal

Charlie Morgan hit headlines back in 2013 after a clash with Eden Hazard, and is set to make an absolute fortune away from the world of football

View Image Charlie Morgan was seemingly kicked by Eden Hazard (Image: Michael Steele, Getty Images)

The ex-Swansea City ballboy who was kicked by Eden Hazard is set to make £500million, 13 years after the infamous incident. Charlie Morgan was embroiled in confrontation with Hazard during the Swans' League Cup semi-final clash with Chelsea in January 2013.

‌



At the age of 17 at the time, he refused to five the ball back to the Belgian winger after it had crossed the line for a goal kick, lying on it with his stomach. That prompted Hazard to attempt to kick it free from underneath him.

‌



That ultimately sparked fury, given Hazard seemed to have made contact with the teenager at the time. As Morgan lay holding his ribs with a frown on his face, referee Chris Foy sent Hazard off.

‌

He accumulated tens of thousands of followers across social media as a result. Yet, more than a decade after the incident, he has carved out success beyond football.

Now 30, the Swansea native co-owns drinks brand Au Vodka, which he established with his friend Jackson Quinn in 2015. Throughout the past decade, the premium vodka label has experienced extraordinary growth, with the company previously valued at approximately £150 million.

Sports.title: Ian Machado Garry confronts UFC rival just moments after Islam Makhachev loss
Sports.content:
Ian Machado Garry confronts UFC rival just moments after Islam Makhachev loss

Machado Garry nearly found himself involved in another clash just moments after going 25 minutes with welterweight champion Islam Makhachev

View Image Ian Machado Garry confronted UFC rival Michael Morales just moments after his loss to Islam Makhachev

Ian Machado Garry was involved in a rather tense backstage face-off with UFC rival Michael Morales just moments after his loss to Islam Makhachev.

‌



The Dublin scrapper fell short in his first shot at UFC gold on Saturday night at UFC 330. Machado Garry, 28, showed glimpses in the third round, but ultimately, Makhachev's championship experience paid dividends. The welterweight king would go on to get the nod on all three of the judges' scorecards.

‌



After going 25 minutes with the men's pound-for-pound number one, Machado Garry was almost involved in another dust-up just minutes later. As the 28-year-old made his way backstage, the Irishman bumped into fellow welterweight star Morales. Several words were exchanged before the pair eventually shook hands and parted ways.

‌



"All the s*** you talk... it's ok. You make sure you back it up," said Machado Garry. "I don't know whatever story you made up about meeting me... I've never encountered that story. Listen, you are a good fighter. Show up. Keep winning and you can do anything. You have got massive fights in this division.

In this sport, if people talk s***, I ignore. Spread good, do good. You have knocked people out, you beat people up, that's what gets respect."

Morales remains undefeated in 19 professional fights, and looks set to be next in line for a crack at Makhachev's coveted gold strap. The 27-year-old knockout artist announced his name on the world stage in his last outing after stopping Sean Brady in the first round last November.

Sports.title: Dana White tears into Ian Machado Garry with brutal five-word assessment
Sports.content:
Dana White tears into Ian Machado Garry with brutal five-word assessment

UFC boss Dana White did not hold back in his assessment of Ian Machado Garry immediately after the Irishman's defeat to Islam Makhachev on Saturday night

View Image UFC boss Dana White was left stunned by Ian Machado Garry during his fight with Islam Makhachev (Image: Zuffa LLC via Getty Images)

UFC supremo Dana White was left far from impressed with Ian Machado Garry's antics heading into the final round of the Irishman's fight with Islam Makhachev.

‌



The Dublin scrapper took on Makhachev in his first title fight in the UFC on Saturday night over in Philadelphia. Makhachev would go on to dominate the majority of the early proceedings, but after a spirited comeback in the third and fourth rounds, the title contest was neck and neck in the final round.

‌



Rather than attempt to stamp his authority in the fifth stanza, Machado Garry rushed to the centre of the canvas and hugged his rival before they eventually split and traded leather for the final five minutes. It was the Russian champion who would go on to get the nod on points - his first successful defence as a 170lb champion.

‌



But boss White was not happy with Machado Garry's respectful gesture at all. "I think Ian is a talented guy. If he had even an ounce of killer instinct, in that fifth round, you don't come out and hug and shake hands. That s*** drives me crazy. You come out in that fifth round with a flying knee and try to finish the fight," he said at the post-fight press conference.

The Russian brawler made history at UFC 330 after he broke Anderson Silva's record for the longest win streak in UFC history (17). Speaking about the historic victory with Khabib Nurmagomedov in his corner, Makhachev said: “Ian is a great fighter, he gave me a hard time. But I prove every fight.

Sports.title: Seven players will miss Arsenal vs Man City Community Shield final
Sports.content:
Seven players will miss Arsenal vs Man City Community Shield final

Arsenal and Manchester City face injury concerns ahead of the Community Shield at Cardiff's Millennium Stadium

View 2 Images William Saliba and Jurrien Timber will miss the Community Shield for Arsenal. (Image: Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Premier League champions Arsenal take on FA Cup holders Manchester City as the top-flight curtain-raiser takes place in Cardiff. Enzo Maresca begins a new dawn in the North West after replacing serial-winner Pep Guardiola.

‌



The Italian returns to management after his shock departure from Chelsea at the beginning of 2026. Maresca enjoyed success in West London and will be hoping to get his latest managerial chapter off to a winning start.

‌



Mikel Arteta will be standing in the opposing dugout looking to put an end to that, to continue the trophy-winning feeling at the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners endured a disappointing end to a famous season, losing to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties but the Community Shield poses new possibilities for the Spaniard.

‌



Man City and Arsenal handed Ayyoub Bouaddi transfer update with coach admission READ MORE :

England star Djed Spence completes Tottenham exit after shining at World Cup READ MORE :

The North American World Cup has disrupted pre-season preparations for clubs across Europe, with star players returning at various intervals.

Arsenal's Premier League victory marked the third trophy during Arteta's tenure at the Emirates Stadium but the first since the FA Cup and subsequent Community Shield triumph in 2020.

The Spaniard has welcomed the confirmation that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are set to feature in the capital.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

However, it's not all positive for the Gunners with crucial defenders William Saliba and Jurrien Timber anticipated to be unavailable. Saliba has been ruled out after the Frenchman's World Cup campaign was cut short by a long-term back problem, which will keep him on the treatment table for a prolonged spell.

Timber has been managing a groin complaint since March, and it proved serious enough to rule him out of the World Cup, despite making a comeback in the closing stages of Arsenal's title-winning campaign, in which they came up short in the Champions League. "Jurrien is progressing really well, he's on the pitch," Arteta said.

‌



"We are ramping up now certain actions and especially the volume and the load. And I think he's in a good trajectory but there's still a few weeks to go.

"I don't know [if he will be back before international break], we have to wait and see. He needs to start to train with the group in the next week or so hopefully and then see how he progresses from there.

"It's been a long-term issue right now and we want to make sure that every step that we take is the right one. He feels right to do that and it's such an important thing for us."

‌



View 2 Images Foes Gabriel and Erling Haaland could reignite their feud at Wembley. (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Rodri made his return to England this week following Spain's exploits, though the Man City midfielder required minor back surgery in the aftermath of Luis de la Fuente's side making history.

The Spaniard's long-term future in the North West remains uncertain, with Barcelona seemingly poised to intensify their pursuit, though this weekend will arrive too soon for the 30-year-old.

‌



Jack Grealish is another City stalwart whose future hangs in the balance following his loan stint at Everton last season. A foot injury, however, cut short his time with the Toffees and he has spent time since recovering from the problem.

The 39-time England international recently returned to training, though he looks unlikely to feature under the famous arch. Ryan McAidoo has been involved during pre-season, but a setback appears set to limit his participation.

The City departures remain up in the air with Maresca's team reportedly bracing for something of a summer clearout. Savinho is another amid interest from Tottenham Hotspur.

Article continues below

The Italian head coach expressed doubts about his availability due to illness, stating: "He was not part of the session [on Thursday], he was a little bit ill.

"We'll see today, the session is in the afternoon, so we'll see how he is today and we'll decide [whether he is available vs Arsenal]."

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso makes Chelsea transfer point with 'last' game warning after Enzo Fernandez deadline
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso makes Chelsea transfer point with 'last' game warning after Enzo Fernandez deadline

Chelsea beat Real Sociedad 3-1 in their final pre-season friendly as eyes turn to the start of the Premier League

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has sent a transfer hint following Chelsea's final pre-season game. (Image: Ryan Pierse, Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has said that some Chelsea players may have played their 'last' game in the pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad. The Spanish side visited Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon as Chelsea finished their season preparations.

‌



The Blues came out as 3-1 winners thanks to goals from Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro (x2). The team are next back in action on Monday as they make the short journey to Craven Cottage to take on Fulham.

‌



A lot of eyes at Stamford Bridge were on Enzo Fernandez. The midfielder made his first appearance of pre-season after an extended break due to the World Cup, but was booed by sections of the home crowd as he came on as a second-half substitute.

‌

There has been a lot of speculation around the Argentine's future, which led to the club establishing a deadline for suitors to meet their £120million valuation. That window closed without the club receiving any offers.

After the match, Alonso delivered his verdict of the game to club channels, where he dropped a transfer suggestion regarding some players who featured in the contest. "It was a very good last preparation game," he said.

Sports.title: 'I would've taken a bullet for Man Utd but I'm not upset that I left - it wasn't the same'
Sports.content:
'I would've taken a bullet for Man Utd but I'm not upset that I left - it wasn't the same'

One Manchester United hero admitted the reasons why he wasn't upset by his Old Trafford departure

View 3 Images Javier Hernandez won two Premier League titles with Manchester United (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Javier Hernandez revealed his lack of sadness at leaving Manchester United was due to the significant change he witnessed at the club. The 38-year-old was largely an unknown commodity when signing for United in 2010 from boyhood club Guadalajara.

‌



However, the Mexican striker soon endeared himself to the fans by scoring 20 goals in 45 games in his first season as United captured the Premier League title. His potency in front of goal, never-say-die attitude and remarkable aerial ability despite his diminutive figure clinched his cult hero status at Old Trafford before his exit in 2015.

‌



His lack of playing time under David Moyes spelled the beginning of the end for Hernandez, who joined Real Madrid on loan in 2014. He was then made surplus to requirements by Louis van Gaal a year later and clinched a £7m move to Bayer Leverkusen.

‌



It's been over a decade since he left Manchester and Hernandez has now opened up about his departure during his appearance on Rio Ferdinand Presents. Speaking to his former United team-mate, the Atletico Dallas striker said: "It was very hard.

"Because if you gave me the chance to stay at United for most of my career, I would have taken it. The team that I played the most games for, even more than my hometown team in Mexico, is United.

"It wasn’t the same club. With the departure, obviously, of Sir Alex Ferguson, but also David Gill and all that family structure. When I say family, it doesn’t mean that it was all nice, but there were values."
