World.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to enter Spanish North African exclave Ceuta
World.content:
The attempted crossings come two weeks after around 72,000 people rushed into the Spanish North African exclave from Morocco. Calls for another mass crossing had been circulating on social media this week.

Moroccan police on Saturday detained dozens of people who attempted to cross the border into the Spanish North African exclave of Ceuta.

It comes two weeks after around 72,000 migrants surged into Ceuta, which drove a wedge between Spain and other EU countries.

"This is a routine operation aimed at preventing attempted irregular migration" toward Ceuta, an official with knowledge of the intervention, who asked to remain anonymous, told AFP.

More than 100 migrants, mostly from sub-Saharan Africa, were stopped in or around Fnideq, the Moroccan city across the border from Ceuta, a security source told Reuters.

Meanwhile, Morocco's Le360 media outlet reported that 294 people had been detained.

Why young Moroccans risked everything to reach Ceuta To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Calls on social media for mass crossings

Earlier this week, Rabat said it was monitoring "the circulation of social media posts and messages of unknown origin" calling for a mass crossing on August 15, and warned that both organizers and participants would face prosecution.

Eyewitnesses said there was a heavy Moroccan security presence around Ceuta and Melilla, another Spanish exclave to the east.

Numerous checkpoints were set up, with patrol boats monitoring the coast and water cannons stationed at the border, according to Spain's public broadcaster RTVE.

Spain's Ceuta grapples with aftermath of border chaos To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Spanish media ordered to leave Fnideq

Spain's EFE news agency and RTVE said a representative from Morocco's Interior Ministry had ordered their journalists ​to leave Fnideq — known in Spanish as Castillejos — immediately without any explanation. The Moroccan official stated that he was "following instructions."

EFE president Miguel Angel Oliver urged Moroccan authorities to respect the free, "responsible and rigorous practice of journalism."

RTVE president Jose Pablo Lopez also demanded "full guarantees and the utmost respect" from Moroccan authorities so that his journalists could "freely practice their profession anywhere in the border region."

"The expulsion of our professionals from Castillejos represents a grave obstacle to press freedom and the right to information," Lopez said in a statement .

Did Morocco instigate the Ceuta migrant incident? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Spain increases security after Ceuta border surge

Two weeks ago, around 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta over a few days, though most have since been returned to Morocco.

Some 100 people had died during the border surge.

Madrid has since beefed up security in the exclave, installing a maritime barrier and deploying more than 500 additional police from mainland Spain.

The Interior Ministry said they would remain in place as long as needed.

"We'll continue to deploy whatever personnel are necessary to restore normality ‌as soon ​as possible and prevent events like those of July 30 from happening again," Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said on Thursday.

World.title: El turismo, la fábrica de oportunidades de España
World.content:
Con cerca de 700.000 empresas y un récord de visitantes en el horizonte, el sector de los viajes, el alojamiento y el ocio premia a los emprendedores que se especializan en un nicho del mercado, buscan soluciones digitales o convierten la sostenibilidad en una ventaja competitiva

Si hay una industria proclive al emprendimiento ahora mismo en España, esa es la del turismo. Este boyante sector, uno de los principales motores económicos nacionales, no para de batir sus propias cifras. Este año se prevé que se acerque a los 100 millones de visitantes —después de alcanzar los 96,8 millones en 2025—, algo nunca visto en el segundo país más visitado del mundo, solo por detrás de Francia. Y ese volumen inédito, explica David Hernández, fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea, genera oportunidades de negocio en toda la cadena de valor: desde los alojamientos a la restauración, el ocio y el transporte.

Triunfar en el sector, asegura Asier Baquero, director del máster en Innovación en Turismo de la Universidad Internacional de La Rioja (UNIR), requiere, no obstante, de estrategia. “Hoy no basta con montar un hotel y esperar a que lleguen los huéspedes; el crecimiento también ha multiplicado la competitividad, por lo que resulta esencial diferenciarse para destacar”, explica el experto. Algo que se consigue a través de la adopción de soluciones innovadoras, de la especialización o de la atención a la creciente sensibilidad de los visitantes por la sostenibilidad.

Consejo de empresario Para emprender hay que ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya, te puedes llevar sorpresas David Hernández, Fundador de la agencia de viajes personalizados Pangea

Digitalización para abrirse camino en el mercado

Las soluciones digitales se han convertido en una palanca de diferenciación en el sector del turismo. Hoy la mayoría de las empresas de éxito nacen en el ecosistema de start-ups para ofrecer soluciones directamente al consumidor. Es el caso de la barcelonesa ByHours, que comercializa habitaciones por horas en hoteles de todo el mundo, o el de la madrileña Civitatis, que ha revolucionado el mercado de las actividades turísticas en español al programar visitas guiadas y excursiones por ciudades de Europa, Latinoamérica, Estados Unidos y Asia. “Ambas han identificado una necesidad del turista y han aportado una solución digital que, además, se puede exportar a cualquier parte del globo”, puntualiza Baquero, que da una pista de por dónde puede ir el emprendimiento: “El objetivo de España ya no es atraer más a turistas, sino gestionar de manera más eficiente la estancia de los que visitan el país”.

Otras empresas de ese ecosistema digital, explica Baquero, se crean con el objetivo de brindar soluciones a las grandes agencias de viajes o a las cadenas hoteleras. “Así sucede con los asistentes de inteligencia artificial para centralitas que gestionan las llamadas de los hoteles y las conectan con las reservas, algo que les permite ahorrar muchos recursos”, explica Baquero.

Jugar la baza de la especialización y la sostenibilidad

Encontrar una solución para un grupo concreto de consumidores es otra de las maneras de empezar con buen pie en el sector. Baquero afirma que hoy los hoteles o las agencias de viaje necesitan un apellido: “Un hotel burbuja, una agencia de viajes de lujo o para el segmento LGTBIQ+...”, ejemplifica el experto. Esta es una de las razones que explica el éxito de Nomading Camp, una empresa especializada en alojamientos de lujo en entornos naturales, con propuestas como suites y habitaciones burbuja en cinco destinos, desde los Pirineos hasta la sierra malagueña de Ronda. Lo justifica su fundador, Miquel Vila: “En nuestro caso, la experiencia es muy importante. No ofrecemos solo una cama, sino una noche en pleno bosque con todas las comodidades. La propia habitación es la experiencia. Nuestros clientes no nos escogen porque quieren ir a un destino y necesitan un sitio para dormir, sino que primero escogen nuestra experiencia y luego se desplazan hasta donde van a vivirla”, describe el empresario.

Emprender en el turismo tiene una dificultad añadida frente a otros sectores: no se venden productos, sino experiencias. Un fabricante puede controlar casi todas las características de lo que produce, pero una empresa turística depende de multitud de factores que determinan cómo recordará el cliente su viaje: la atención, el clima, las expectativas del viajero, la coordinación entre distintos servicios... Por eso, el éxito no consiste solo en ofrecer un buen servicio, sino en conseguir que el visitante viva una experiencia que merezca la pena recomendar, defiende Hernández, de Pangea. “Vendemos viajes a destinos cercanos, pero también a 10.000 kilómetros de distancia, con 20 proveedores, por lo que hay una alta probabilidad de que algo salga mal”, destaca.

Consejo de empresario Sigue tu propio camino sin fijarte en el camino de otros emprendedores Miquel Vila, fundador de los alojamientos de lujo en plena naturaleza Nomading Camp

La sostenibilidad gana cada vez más peso como ventaja en esta industria, asegura Baquero. Porque no solo responde a una creciente demanda de los viajeros, sino que también contribuye a reducir costes, acceder a financiación y cumplir la normativa. Por eso cada vez más compañías deciden que su propuesta de valor esté claramente ligada a la sostenibilidad, la economía circular o la conservación del entorno. La catalana Turismo Vivencial se ha hecho un hueco en el mercado ofreciendo consultoría sobre ecoturismo, el turismo respetuoso con el medio ambiente, y organiza actividades que contribuyen a conservar el patrimonio natural y cultural, así como generar beneficios a las comunidades locales. Cada vez son más comunes las compañías que ayudan a negocios del sector a medir su impacto ambiental, como la valenciana Bioscore Sustainability y la madrileña GreeMKO, que no es exclusiva del sector turístico, pero desarrolla programas para la gestión ambiental y el cálculo automatizado de la huella de carbono de hoteles.

Lecciones de los emprendedores

David Hernández y Miquel Vila, que protagonizan el último capítulo de El poder de las empresas, el pódcast de los que hacen , de Banco Sabadell, comparten algunas de las lecciones que han aprendido después de emprender y que pueden ser de utilidad para los empresarios de hoy y mañana. Vila, de Nomading Camp, asegura que, con el tiempo y la distancia, le hubiera gustado compararse menos con otros emprendedores y haber hecho caso a su instinto más frecuentemente: “Merece la pena seguir tu propio camino. Por ejemplo, si tus competidores están haciendo rondas de inversión y tú sientes que no necesitas una nueva, no la hagas; tu gran meta ha de ser que tu negocio funcione, no la ronda en sí misma”. Hernández, de Pangea, señala una actitud como clave a la hora de enfrentarse a cualquier decisión: “No hay que ser demasiado optimista. Me explico: creo que para ser emprendedor es imprescindible ser optimista, pero si te pasas de la raya luego te puedes llevar sorpresas”.

World.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
World.content:
Vielha (Lleida). La gran baza de los pueblos seleccionados radica, sobre todo, en la posibilidad de tener que taparse para descansar, algo que se ha convertido en todo un lujo durante la canícula. Es un requisito que cumple Vielha, a la vera de los ríos Garona y Nere, con su casco histórico construido a la manera aranesa, a golpe de piedra, pizarra y madera. Sus mínimas descenderán hasta los 12ºC la noche del domingo; las máximas alcanzarán picos de 33ºC en las horas centrales del jueves y viernes, pero bajarán a los 24ºC (y con probabilidad de lluvias) el lunes, según la Aemet. La capital del Valle de Arán se presenta como un buen campamento base para conocer este territorio del Pirineo catalán, con sus 33 núcleos de población, sus algo más de 10.000 habitantes y sus iglesias románicas. Es recomendable acercarse a la cascada Saut deth Pish, probablemente la más bonita de la zona. Más información: visitvaldaran.com/descubre-la-val-daran/pueblos/vielha/.

Toni M (GETTY IMAGES)

World.title: Hockey World Cup kicks off in Amstelveen with Dutch victory
World.content:
The hockey World Cup has begun, with the Dutch women beating Chile 2-0 in the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen.

Sixteen men’s and 16 women’s teams are competing for the two world titles over the next fortnight. The Netherlands is co-hosting with Belgium, where matches are at the new Belfius Hockey Arena in Wavre, south-east of Brussels.

Both Dutch teams play all five of their group matches at the Wagener Stadium.

The Dutch women

The women’s team is the clear favourite. It holds the world, Olympic and European titles and tops the world rankings by a wide margin.

The tournament is the last of Xan de Waard’s career. The 30-year-old midfielder, twice named the world’s best player, announced in the spring that she would retire afterwards.

De Waard has won all three World Cups she has played in, in 2014, 2018 and 2022. According to NOS, no hockey player, male or female, has won four.

“I think we are always the favourites, so we are now as well,” she told the broadcaster.

The Dutch men

The men are Olympic champions but have not won a world title since 1998. They are ranked second in the world behind Belgium.

Their first match is against New Zealand on Sunday at 4pm, and they play Argentina two days later. Prime minister Rob Jetten is due to attend the tournament as a spectator. His partner, Nicolás Keenan, plays for Argentina and for Klein Zwitserland in The Hague.

Where to watch

NOS is showing all the Dutch matches live on NPO 1, on its website and in its app. Tickets are still on sale through the tournament website, including day tickets covering every match at one venue.

The women’s final is at the Wagener Stadium on August 29 and the men’s final is in Wavre the next day.

World.title: Jetten condemns Star of David stickers at farmers’ protest
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has branded it “a disgusting act” that campaign group Farmers Defence Force (FDF) handed out Star of David stickers at Friday’s farmers’ protest in Den Bosch, according to Omroep Brabant.

The stickers show a Star of David in the pattern of a red farmers’ handkerchief, with the letter B for “boer”, or farmer. The star was a reference to the badge Jews were forced to wear under Nazi occupation.

“If you think you can make your point with this, I think you are only damaging your own cause,” Jetten said.

FDF leader Mark van den Oever said the stickers were meant to underline the injustice being done to farmers. Asked whether he thought the comparison with Jews during the WWII was inappropriate, he said revoking permits was also inappropriate.

Van den Oever also told Hart van Nederland permits were revoked in 1938 and that the same was now being done to farmers, that he understood the stickers could hurt people, but that action groups need to cause friction.

CIDI, a Jewish organisation called the comparison baseless and reprehensible. Ronny Naftaniel, a former director of CIDI and former chairman of the Central Jewish Council, said the farmers were undermining their own position by using the symbol.

Farm permits

The protest was called against the provincial executive’s plan to revoke the nature permits of five poultry farms near protected nature areas, which the farmers say would put them out of business.

After a debate lasting most of Friday, the executive said it was provisionally sticking to that plan, and a no-confidence motion against the executive member responsible, Saskia Boelema, was defeated.

Boelema told the council she had sought contact with the five farmers, who had waited eight months for a response to their plans. Broadcaster NOS, which has seen the email she sent to one of them, reported that it was sent two days before the debate.

The only motion to pass tells the executive to meet the farmers as soon as possible and to consider alternatives such as keeping fewer animals or relocating. A formal decision is due on October 1. Two people died on Friday morning in a crash on the A59, at the back of a queue that had built up as tractors drove to the protest.

World.title: Shell and Philips hit by Russian ransomware attack
World.content:
The Russia-linked ransomware group Cl0p claims to have hacked global corporations Shell and Philips. The two are among nearly 50 companies Cl0p has listed on its website, alongside General Electric and payments firm Fiserv.

From the oil giant, the group says it has taken some 89 gigabytes of material, including technical drawings, facility images, scans of test reports and project plans. They claimed to have stolen another 13.5 gigabytes from health technology company Philips, mostly diagrams and blueprints.

Both companies are investigating, with Shell saying it is “aware of a possible incident”.

Philips said it had “identified and contained an attempted cybersecurity compromise of a specific enterprise server related to internal data”. A spokesperson told NOS that the incident is now under control and has no impact on its customers.

Russian hackers

Cl0p, which has been active since 2019, is a Russia-linked ransomware group that has likely already extorted $500 million from other victims.

It operates by stealing files and other sensitive data from companies and then threatens to publish them online unless a ransom is paid.

There’s no word yet on how much money the hackers are asking for in exchange for not selling or releasing the stolen data.

Security researchers have linked the campaign to a flaw in Windchill, engineering software made by American firm PTC, which was patched on June 17. Neither Shell nor Philips has said how it was breached.

Writing about the attacks, TNW editor-in-chief Ana-Maria Stanciuc said the pattern carried an uncomfortable lesson: “When enough of the corporate world standardises on the same enterprise platform, one shared supplier quietly becomes everyone’s single point of failure, and no amount of internal security spending can fully patch a hole in someone else’s code.”

World.title: Jetten tells farmers to get off motorways after two die in crash
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has said it is “unacceptable” that tractors were driving on the A59 motorway on Friday, after two people were killed and six injured in a crash. The collision happened at the back of a queue that had built up as the tractors drove to a protest in Den Bosch.

“It is unacceptable and incomprehensible to demonstrate on the motorway because it leads to very dangerous situations,” Jetten said during a press conference.

Jetten also said the decision not to stop the tractors earlier was not a good signal and would have to be reviewed. News agency ANP reported that 50 tractors were driving on the A2 towards Utrecht as he spoke. “Don’t do it, get off the motorway,” Jetten said.

Police said four cars were involved and that they were still investigating what caused the collision, but no tractors were involved.

The victims have not been identified. The tractors had been in the right-hand lane and other traffic could pass on the left, but a traffic jam still built up.

Disputed agreements

Tractors are not permitted on Dutch motorways. Earlier this week the public prosecution department (OM) and the police said they would not stop farmers who drove onto them, citing the right to demonstrate.

A spokesperson for the OM in Oost-Brabant told broadcaster NOS that this had not been agreed. The authorities help demonstrations go ahead, the spokesperson said, but once a tractor is on the motorway it is up to the local mayor, police and prosecutors to decide when and how to step in.

“A tractor on the motorway is never allowed, and is a criminal offence” the spokesperson said. The OM did not answer questions from NOS about what had been agreed instead, or why nobody intervened.

Provincial council members held a minute’s silence for the two dead. Mark van den Oever of Farmers Defence Force called on farmers at the provincial offices not to travel home by motorway.

What the protest is about

Noord-Brabant’s provincial executive intends to revoke the nature permits of five poultry farms close to protected nature areas, after environmental groups won a court case in April 2025.

The court found the protected areas were overloaded with nitrogen, and that the farms were a significant cause. But it stopped short of ordering the permits withdrawn, giving the province, the farmers and the environmental groups a year to come up with a plan that would cut nitrogen levels for good.

The farmers sent in their plans in November 2025 but in July were told their permits would be revoked, although that decision is not yet final. The provincial executive has admitted it never gave them a proper response to those plans, Omroep Brabant reported.

Members of the provincial council, which oversees the executive, broke off their summer break on Friday for a debate on the plan demanded by seven opposition parties, led by farmers’ party BBB. Saskia Boelema, the executive member responsible, told them the province should have sat down with the farmers earlier and apologised for the way the process had been handled.

World.title: Mouse invasion plagues Friesland farmers
World.content:
A mouse plague has been destroying fields in Friesland in the northwest of the country, depleting crops as the rodents eat entire patches of land.

According to Omrop Fryslân, recent weeks have seen the mice mostly causing damage in peat meadows, but they have now also infiltrated clay areas.

“They eat the roots and then the grass dies,” farmer Jan Brouwer from Koufurderrige told the broadcaster. He estimates that it reduces his grass yield by up to 20%.

Drought

The outbreak comes on the heels of a countrywide drought, which has also affected the farmers.

But as there’s no irrigation ban in Friesland yet as compared to other areas of the country, Brouwer was able to flood his fields to flush out the mice. The critters drown in their burrows, and those that try to escape are easy prey for birds.

The water has also helped his land come back to life. “We were making silage today and the grass is starting to come back quite nicely in those spots,” said Brouwer.

The nearby Ijsselmeer still has plenty of water, but that could change if the drought persists.

There have been several mouse plagues since 2015 in the region. And with them, comes an owl invasion, including the short-eared owl. “I have seen at least six short-eared owls here in the past few weeks,” says Brouwer.

Researchers expect the number of mice to decrease substantially next year. “With such a plague, at a certain point there are simply too many,” said Niek Bosma of the regional waterboard. “Then a disease sets in, and within a few weeks all those mice are dead.”

But a few ultimately remain, meaning another mouse plague is inevitable.

World.title: Care homes, prisons and asylum centres hit by night-time heat
World.content:
As daytime temperatures continue to soar during the Netherlands’ fifth heatwave this year, night-time heat, where temperatures stay above 20 degrees, has lagged behind in public discourse despite its effects on the population.

“Night-time heat is an under-examined aspect of heatwaves,” Lisette Klok, researcher at the Climate Adaptation Services foundation, told broadcaster NOS and NRC.

Especially for vulnerable people – including the elderly and those living in asylum seeker centres and prisons – “night-time temperature is important because your body needs the chance to recover from the heat at night. Poor sleep [due to the heat] makes that more difficult.”

Hot nights, which are defined from 11pm to 7am, affect how well people are able to cope during daytime heat. People tend to sleep worse, making them less functional during the day. In addition, homes build up heat because they can’t cool down during the night, meaning neither do their inhabitants.

Climate atlas

The foundation puts out the Climate Impact Atlas, which maps climate effects – from threats of flooding, waterlogging, drought and heat – throughout the country. Using the Atlas, NRC and regional broadcasters found that on average, there are some six tropical nights per year in the Netherlands, although there are regional differences.

Going neighborhood by neighborhood, the journalists found that in parts of South Limburg, there is an average of 15 “sticky nights” annually.

Maastricht has the most hot nights in the country, while the Randstad also has a higher number. The north of the Netherlands sees less than the national average. Urban areas also take a heat hit, with city centres becoming “heat islands” on hot days. Heat in these areas is even worse at night.

“As a result, homes can be cooled less effectively by ventilation,” said Marjolein van Esch, urban microclimate researcher at TU Delft. “This depends on the difference in air temperature between indoors and outdoors. The greater that difference, the easier it is to cool. Due to the urban heat island effect, that temperature difference is smaller.”

Elderly

The high night-time temperatures have a particularly strong effect on older people, who are more vulnerable to heat.

That led some nursing homes being evacuated earlier this summer, including the De Taling care home in Den Bosch and a facility in Raalte whose systems temporarily failed in July.

“Many buildings are designed for a different climate,” a spokesperson for the care organization Carinova told NOS. “The climate systems were tested to the limit at some locations this summer.”

Temporary portable air conditioners and moving residents to cooler rooms helped ease the problems.

Asylum seekers and prisoners

Since 2021, new homes must meet certain requirements to prevent overheating, but the rules don’t apply to existing houses and also usually not to care homes, prisons and asylum seeker centres. Requirements also vary depending on the region.

But residents of asylum seeker centres and prisons, who have nowhere else to go, are not allowed to install air conditioners on their own. Refugee settlement agency COA allows only one fan per room.

According to NRC, the Dutch Correctional Institutions Agency said increasing temperatures in prisons in recent years mean it needs more resources to cool things down. “Many buildings are due for major maintenance or renovation.”

World.title: Fifth heatwave confirmed as temperatures reach 37°
World.content:
Temperatures will reach 37° on Friday, after forecaster Weeronline confirmed the fifth regional heatwave of the year.

Temperatures will range from 33° in the north to 37° in the south and southeast, the national weather service KNMI said.

Five heatwaves in a single year have happened only once before, in 1947. Then it was Maastricht alone – this year several southern stations have reached the tally.

There will be no national heatwave, which is measured at the KNMI station in De Bilt, near Utrecht. Most of the country, including the Randstad and the north, will fall below the threshold.

KNMI has issued a code yellow warning for heat across the country. The national heat plan, run by public health institute RIVM, puts care homes and health services on alert. It covers the whole country on Friday and only the southeast on Saturday.

Friday night will stay warm, with temperatures holding near 20° in towns and cities.

Saturday will be cooler, with a chance of thunderstorms, although the southeast may still reach about 32°. Sunday will peak at 24°, and next week will be cooler and wetter, with maximums of 21 to 25° and rain likely from Tuesday.

The weekend rain will do little for the drought. Weeronline says short showers run off ground that is baked too hard to absorb water.

World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among the thousands to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue, which weighs around 60,000 tons, took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mold into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. The proportion of children taking Catholic catechism in schools has continued to fall but remains a majority https://t.co/5bu35hzJ7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has only a majority of nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland hit by theft of 19 million patients’ data from medical platform
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The personal data of almost 19 million people, including medical information, has been compromised in a major cyberattack on a company that provides services to thousands of medical facilities in Poland. “We are dealing with one of the largest incidents in Poland’s history,” said digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski on Wednesday. He urged people to use government services to check whether their data is affected and to “lock” their national identity number to prevent potential fraud. (￼🧵 1/2) 💬 Dziś doszło do poważnego wycieku danych w firmie MyDr, który może obejmować blisko 19 milionów osób korzystających z opieki medycznej. W związku z sytuacją krytyczną zostały natychmiast podjęte działania mające zabezpieczyć dane i wyjaśnić okoliczności incydentu –… pic.twitter.com/nIp6EvbKiu — Ministerstwo Cyfryzacji (@CYFRA_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The attack targeted MyDr, a company that provides services used by many medical facilities in Poland. Its data includes patients’ personal information, as well as medical details such as diagnoses and prescriptions. It was first reported on Monday by Zaufana Trzecia Strona, an IT security news service, which said that it had been contacted on Saturday by the alleged perpetrators, who claimed to have accessed the data of around 18.8 million people. The hackers, who have not been identified, had also sent a screenshot from the compromised database showing the personal data of “one of the most important politicians in Poland”, added Zaufana Trzecia Strona. Shortly afterwards, MyDr confirmed that it had “become the target of an external, deliberate criminal activity involving some of our data”. In an update on Wednesday, it said that, at the time of writing, there was no evidence that the data had been published anywhere. Największy wyciek danych osobowych w historii Polski i co możemy z nim zrobić – nasza analiza incydentu w MyDr i jego potencjalnych skutków.https://t.co/vXUmVfpPAP Opisujemy aktualny stan wiedzy i możliwe scenariusze rozwoju sytuacji. pic.twitter.com/uqhjz1CjZ1 — ZaufanaTrzeciaStrona @zaufanatrzeciastrona@infosec (@Zaufana3Strona) August 13, 2026 Gawkowski addressed the issue at a press briefing on Wednesday. He noted that “there is no indication we are dealing with an external attack…from Russia or any other country”. Poland has recently regularly been targetted by Russian state-linked hackers. It is “very likely” that cybercriminals are behind the attack on MyDr, said Gawkowski, who pledged that there would be an “uncompromising” response from the Polish security services. The minister advised Poles to check in a secure government database whether their data had been leaked. He also advised citizens to use the state web portal, known as mObywatel, to “lock” their identity number, known as a PESEL, which prevents fraudsters from using it. Around 12,000 medical facilities use MyDr’s services, the digital affairs ministry told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The company claims that it processes three million medical consultations and 2.7 million prescriptions a month, reports the Gazeta Wyborcza daily.
